verdict.rationale: Semgrep Secrets clearly detects hardcoded/exposed credentials in the current codebase (semgrep-docs-8, semgrep-docs-9) and pre-commit integration is recommended specifically to keep secrets out of git history (semgrep-docs-16), but no evidence shows Semgrep itself scanning the full git commit history for previously-committed secrets (a capability tools like gitleaks/trufflehog provide) — its docs and CLI examples focus on scanning the working tree/repo state, not historical commits. Missing for 10: documentation or CLI flag for scanning entire git history/past commits for secrets, and independent confirmation of that capability.
